To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PID based force feedback control of a nonlinear, four DOF, half-car AVSS, is a simple, effective, and robust method for reducing the vehicle body vertical acceleration and the suspension travel.
the two-loop, PID based, AVSS is capable of improving the ride comfort and handling performance of an active vehicle suspension system, when compared to a passive suspension system.

the two-loop PID control of a nonlinear, four DOF, half-car active suspension model, is effective at reducing the suspension displacement, body acceleration, and road input force, when compared to a passive half-car suspension system, with the same model parameter values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an AVSS with PID controllers for a half-car vehicle model, which is a simplified model of a full car.
the development of an effective, robust and simple control system for AVSSs.
the development of a two-loop PID controller to improve the ride and handling performance of the half-car AVSS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PID control system is capable of providing the required performance in the presence of deterministic disturbance.
the AVSS with PID control is superior to the passive suspension system in ride comfort, road handling and tire contact force.
the PID based AVS system is a good choice for the control of the active suspension system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PID force control loop is a viable solution for the control of the AVSS, and the PID suspension control loop is a suitable candidate to improve the performance of a PID based AVSS.
the PID force/suspension control system is an effective control system to improve the performance of a nonlinear, half-car, AVSS.
the PID control system is an effective method for the AVSS design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple PID control scheme can provide a significant performance improvement in a nonlinear AVSS.

the two-loop PID based active suspension system is capable of providing the same ride comfort level and the same vehicle body displacement as the nonlinear passive system, while maintaining the vehicle body displacement and the tire deflection within the allowable range.
the PID control scheme can be used as a viable alternative to more complicated and expensive control schemes for active suspension control of vehicles.
